newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Ex-U.N. chief, Israeli elected to jurists' body.
newsitem.headline: Ex-U.N. chief, Israeli elected to jurists' body.

text.p: Former United Nations Secretary General Boutros Boutros-Ghali was on Tuesday elected an honorary member of the International Commission of Jurists (ICJ), an independent body that works to promote the rule of law.
A statement from the Geneva-based organisation said prominent Israeli human rights activist Ruth Gavison, professor of law at Hebrew University in Jerusalem, had been elected a member of the ICJ.
Boutros-Ghali, also a former deputy prime minister for foreign affairs of Egypt, stepped down from the U.N. post at the end of last year after the United States insisted he had to go.
He had served as a full member of the ICJ, founded in 1952 to work for full observance around the world of the provisions of the U.N. Declaration of Human Rights, from 1973-81.

The ICJ said Gavison, also president of the Association for Civil Liberties in Israel, "has had a long association with human rights and the Rule of Law both as an academic and as a legal practitioner."

Composed of a maximum of 45 jurists at any one time, the ICJ has 80 national sections and affiliated organisations. It monitors judicial procedures around the globe and often sends observers to trials that have political undertones.

It has been strongly critical of many Arab countries and of Israel over what it has said were violations of the rule of law, and has published in-depth studies of legal issues including one on the application of the death penalty in the United States.
Its current Secretary-General is Adama Dieng of Senegal.
